clue.text: Atrocious standard set by harangue

parts.note: a standard is a banner or flag
to harangue is to rant at length

explanation.surface: A dreadful benchmark is laid down by someone ranting at a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is a glaring, shocking one, so the word is a synonym of outrageous wrongdoing.

clue.text: A demand for attention

parts.note: an exclamation telling someone to listen to you or watch what you are doing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an interjection used to make someone notice or listen.

clue.text: Doesn't turn to crime

parts.note: literally travelling without turning, and idiomatically living honestly after release from prison

explanation.definitionFit: An ex-offender who lives honestly is said to keep to a direct, unbending course.

clue.text: Intelligence team headed by a copper

indicators.note: headed by means the team comes after, with the other pieces at its head

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a team is a group of men

explanation.surface: A police intelligence unit is led by a constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewdness or keen insight is a form of intelligence.

clue.text: Rang the bell audibly and gave the news

indicators.note: audibly tells us the word for bell-ringing is to be heard, not seen

parts.note: a bell that rang slowly tolled

explanation.surface: A town crier rang his bell and announced the latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone of the news is to relate or report it to them.

clue.text: Working-class symbol worn by the clergy?

definitions.text: Working-class symbol worn by the clergy?

parts.words: Working-class symbol worn by the clergy?
parts.note: the flat headgear of the working man, read as if it were a hat for the clergy, who are known as the cloth

explanation.walkthrough: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy; a flat tweed hat is a traditional British emblem of the working man.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat woollen hat is the traditional emblem of the British working man.

clue.text: Pained expression when top of bed falls off

indicators.note: top of picks out the opening letter of the word for the bed
falls off says that opening letter drops away

parts.note: a couch is a bed or sofa

explanation.surface: Someone yelps when the headboard of their bed falls off.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of pain is a cry or pained utterance.

clue.text: Apprentices the boss sent sprawling

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a knob or raised ornament

indicators.note: sprawling things lie in disorder, so the word sent is jumbled

explanation.surface: The manager sends trainees off in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' is the anagram signal; boss here is the raised knob on a shield or ceiling, not the employer the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Learners still in training are pupils or apprentices.

clue.text: Wholly fair? Not by a long way

parts.note: wholly in the sense of solely or exclusively, i.e. only
fair means just or equitable

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing is completely fair, and the reply is a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not by a long way' looks like a denial, but it defines a narrow margin: winning by a whisker is the opposite of winning by a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achieved barely, by the narrowest margin, is the reverse of a wide victory.

clue.text: One who always talks well

definitions.meaning: a tedious person who talks endlessly
as a noun, a shaft drilled into the ground for water

explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome talker is a classic dullard, and a borehole sunk for water is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: Sort of house in Cheam, its deed is mislaid

indicators.note: a deed that is mislaid is put in the wrong place, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A homeowner in Cheam has lost the title deeds to their property.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEAM is a suburb of south London; its letters with ITS and DEED are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A house joined to one neighbour by a shared wall is a common British type of dwelling.

clue.text: They don't seem to mind life being a continuous drag

definitions.text: They don't seem to mind life being a continuous drag

parts.words: They don't seem to mind life being a continuous drag
parts.note: a drag is a puff on a cigarette, so a life of unbroken puffs describes heavy smokers

explanation.definitionFit: Heavy smokers light one cigarette from the last, so their life is a continuous drag.

clue.text: Guard ordered to breached line

parts.note: to be ordered to a place is to be sent there

indicators.note: a breached line is broken open, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A soldier is commanded to go to a spot where the defensive line has been broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breached' is the anagram signal for the line; 'ordered to' reads as one idea, being sent somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry posted to keep watch is a lookout or guard.

clue.text: A deal with America for plant

parts.note: a deal in the sense of a great amount, a lot
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: An American bargain on some greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A water lily of Asia is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Greek ferry operator casts anchor

indicators.note: casts in the sense of throws about or moulds afresh, so the word anchor is reshaped

explanation.surface: A boatman from Greece drops his anchor overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the ferryman rows the souls of the dead across the river Styx.
explanation.definitionFit: In mythology this figure is the boatman who carries the dead over the Styx, a ferry operator from Greek legend.

clue.text: Gamble with a Greek character

parts.note: to gamble is to bet

explanation.surface: Someone places a wager alongside a man from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet is one of its characters.

clue.text: How slowly one travelled in olden days

definitions.text: How slowly one travelled in olden days

parts.words: How slowly one travelled in olden days
parts.note: stages were stagecoaches, so travel was done in coaches and in short steps

explanation.definitionFit: Gradually, step by step; and in the past journeys were made by stagecoach.

clue.text: Highly likely to win?

parts.note: the phrase for being in the lead also reads literally as being high up, above everything else

explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in the lead is uppermost, both literally high and figuratively winning.

clue.text: Start blazing away — that's what one hopes it will do

definitions.text: that's what one hopes it will do
definitions.meaning: a grate is lit in hope that the flames will catch and burn well in the open hearth

explanation.definitionFit: The order to begin shooting, and also what one hopes a newly lit hearth will become.

clue.text: Crackers — or what they're required for?

definitions.meaning: read crackers as nutcrackers, tools needed for opening hard-shelled kernels

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, and also the hard-shelled fruit a cracker is made to open.

clue.text: Changes course when vessel's caught in the swell

indicators.note: caught in says the vessels are held inside the word for the swell

parts.note: a swell is a toff, a smartly dressed upper-class person
vessels are urns

explanation.surface: A ship alters direction when caught in heavy seas.
explanation.walkthrough: The swell is not the sea but a toff, a posh person; vessel's here is read as plural vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave one road for another is to change course.

clue.text: Pick one out, get one free

definitions.meaning: to pick one person from a group
free in the sense of unmarried or unattached

explanation.definitionFit: To choose one from many, and also unattached or not in a relationship.

clue.text: So my acer tree has had to be transplanted

indicators.note: a transplanted plant is moved into new ground, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener explains that a Japanese maple has had to be moved to a new spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A large maple species common in Britain is a kind of tree.

clue.text: Composer giving many an offer of a lift

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
a driver offering a lift says hop in

explanation.surface: A musician gives lots of people rides in his car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Polish pianist famous for nocturnes is a great composer.

clue.text: A sheaf of corn that comes as a surprise

definitions.meaning: a shock is a stook, a stack of sheaves standing in a field, so one sheaf is part of it

explanation.definitionFit: Literally one sheaf from a stook of corn, and idiomatically something rather surprising.

clue.text: Piece of news I encountered on rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: encountered means met

explanation.surface: Someone hears a bit of news as they get out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A single report in a newspaper is an item.

clue.text: Corporation band

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, so a band worn around it, rather than a council brass band

explanation.walkthrough: Corporation suggests a town council, but it is old humorous slang for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide ribbon worn around the waist is a band round the belly.

clue.text: Return tender love

indicators.note: return asks for the word tender's synonym to be sent back the other way

parts.note: tender means sore or painful to the touch

explanation.surface: A request to send back a tender gesture of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of desire stands for love itself.

clue.text: Inspect damaged roses for blemishes

parts.note: to eye something is to inspect it

indicators.note: damaged roses are knocked out of shape, so the letters of roses are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener examines spoilt roses looking for marks on the petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' is the anagram signal; Inspect is a verb here, as in to look someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly sights that spoil a scene are blots or blemishes on it.

clue.text: Don't contact workers in their free time

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
workers not on duty are off

explanation.surface: An instruction not to phone staff when they are not at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The order to keep away and not touch is an instruction against contact.
